text:
The Avalanche are without Nathan MacKinnon for about a month and Cale Makar for about two weeks (Field Level Media), and Wednesday in Utah showed what that looks like on a bad night: a 4-1 loss, Martin Necas taking a scary hit and another player leaving after a collision in a violent first period (Yahoo Sports). Utah's Liam O'Brien, in the Denver Post via Corey Masisak: "If you touch any of our top guys, me and the boys are coming for you." The teams meet in the Winter Classic, and it already feels like a rivalry.

The good news is the foundation. Colorado is 12-7-3 with 27 points, has 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and our numbers put its record almost exactly where its play says it should be. The playoff odds are 96%. That's a cushion built before the injuries.

What's missing is real. The MacKinnon line with Artturi Lehkonen and Necas had outscored teams 20-10, and Makar with Devon Toews took 60% of the expected goals. The goaltending is the worry: Scott Wedgewood is at .882 and 4.4 goals worse than expected over his last five starts, putting more on Mackenzie Blackwood. The Avs claimed defenseman Mike Reilly to patch the blue line, and Jared Bednar said "we'll see" about when he plays (per Masisak). The next two weeks are about surviving, not dominating.
headline: Colorado's depth test got harder in Utah
